The structure is described in space group No. 109, I4₁md (Hall symbol I 4bw -2), using fractional atomic coordinates. The supplied input cell is not the conventional tetragonal cell: it has equal edge lengths a = b = c = 7.09818871 Å, with interaxial angles α = β = 135.45288969° and γ = 64.82732007°. This nonstandard rhombohedral-like input setting contains eight atoms in total, with the declared input composition Tm₂Ag₂S₄.

The relationship between the supplied input fractional coordinates q_input and the standard fractional coordinates q_standard is given by q_standard = P q_input + s. The transformation matrix P has rows (0.49999999999999994, -0.5, 0.5), (0.5, -0.5000000000000001, -0.5), and (0.5, 0.5, -0.5), while the origin shift s is (5.551115123125783e-17, 0.5, -5.551115123125783e-17). Thus, within numerical roundoff, the standard frame is obtained from the input frame by that linear remapping of the cell axes together with a one-half translation along the second standard fractional axis. Coordinate values are rounded to six decimal places.

In the standard frame, all four independent crystallographic orbits lie on the polar fourfold axis and belong to Wyckoff position 4a, with coordinate relation (0, 0, z). Thulium occupies one 4a orbit with z = 0.753844, giving four symmetry-related Tm positions per conventional cell. Silver occupies a separate 4a orbit with z = 0.21889, also of multiplicity four. Sulfur is distributed over two inequivalent 4a orbits: one has z = 0.982607 and the other has z = 0.5291689999999999, each with multiplicity four. Because these sulfur orbits are crystallographically distinct, both independent z parameters must be retained.

Taken together, the conventional I4₁md description contains four Tm atoms, four Ag atoms, and eight S atoms generated by body-centering and the polar fourfold symmetry operations from the four independent representatives. The smaller supplied input cell instead contains Tm₂Ag₂S₄, corresponding to one quarter of the conventional-cell contents, and its geometry is recovered exactly by applying the stated inverse relationship to the standard-frame coordinates through the given matrix and origin shift.
